selection_reasoning: These four tasks form a coherent multi-hop sequence centered around exploring a spruce-themed structure and interacting with its components. The player must first locate spruce planks (a building material that forms the structure), which leads them to discover a spruce button and spruce door (both made from spruce planks and logically placed on/near the spruce structure). Finally, after navigating through the spruce door, the player reaches and interacts with a stonecutter inside. This creates a natural exploration flow: find the material → find interactive elements on the structure → enter through the door → use the workstation inside. The tasks are observable, verifiable, and don't require deep crafting knowledge.

The spruce door is part of the spruce plank structure; locating the planks building reveals the door entrance
The stonecutter is inside the room accessed through the spruce door; must find and open the door to reach it

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/observe task. The target is the center of the spruce plank building at spawn-relative (0, 2, 13). Max distance 8 means the player must walk at least ~5 blocks forward from spawn (since building center is ~13.2 blocks from origin). Facing tolerance 60° ensures the player is looking at the structure. This is the first milestone to trigger as the player approaches.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/observe task for a small detail block. The spruce button is at (-1, 2, 10) on the front wall. Max distance 5 requires the player to walk to at least z=5 from spawn (button is ~10.3 blocks from origin). Facing tolerance 45° is tighter than other milestones because the button is a small 1-block detail requiring precise visual identification.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/observe task. The spruce door is at (0, 1, 10) on the front wall. Max distance 5 requires the player to walk to at least z=5 from spawn (door is ~10.05 blocks from origin). Facing tolerance 60° allows some lateral viewing angle since the door is a 1x2 block feature that's easier to spot than the button.

Uses position_near_with_facing because interacting with a stonecutter requires the player to be within right-click range and facing it. The stonecutter is inside the building at (0, 1, 13), which is 3 blocks behind the front wall (z=10). Max distance 3 effectively requires the player to be inside the building (must pass through the door at z=10 to reach z≥10, then be within 3 blocks of z=13). This is the best available rule since use_item may not reliably track stonecutter GUI opening.

scene_description: A compact spruce plank workshop building on a grass field, positioned 10 blocks north of spawn. The building has a spruce door entrance on the south wall with a spruce button beside it, glass pane windows on the east and west walls, torches for interior lighting, and a stonecutter workstation in the center of the room. The player spawns facing the building from 10 blocks away, requiring navigation to approach and explore.
task_text: Explore the area to find a spruce plank building. Locate the spruce button and spruce door on the front wall, then enter through the door and interact with the stonecutter inside.
design_notes: Building front wall at z=10, back wall at z=16. Door at (0,1,10), button at (-1,2,10), stonecutter at (0,1,13). Player spawns at origin facing north. Distance from spawn to front wall is 10 blocks — requires meaningful navigation. Building is 7x7 blocks footprint with 5x5 interior. Glass pane windows on east/west walls allow peeking inside. Two torches light the interior.
